defenses.response: Agreed, and I commit to this explicitly rather than leaving it implied. Every surviving draft (response letter r3#2, the Discussion G9 paragraph, and the todo/040 registration amendment) will state, in this order: (1) the originally registered targets (~0 FITTED, ~-0.5 Bayesian draw), (2) the measured results and their misses (+0.853 at ~5.3 se from 0; +0.628 at ~7 se from -0.5, wrong sign), (3) only then the mechanical finding that Bernoulli's entropy is parameter-dependent (escapes the known-scale collapse), labeled explicitly as a post-hoc correction of a registration error, not a restatement of the original prediction.
defenses.amendment: Add a verbatim requirement to the write-up: state the original target and its miss BEFORE any corrected framing, in every one of the three documents (response letter, G9, todo/040 amendment).
defenses.residual_risk: None once the amendment is applied and verified against the actual file text.

defenses.response: This objection is correct and I will not claim more than the math supports. The entropy-gradient calculation (dH/dp = -logit(p) != 0 generically) is airtight for one thing only: it shows Bernoulli's own conditional missing-data entropy is NOT parameter-free, which is the theorem's own stated NECESSARY condition for the known-scale collapse to apply -- so Bernoulli demonstrably does not fall in that special case. It does NOT by itself establish that the general theorem's full regularity conditions (R1-R7, stated and verified in the multivariate-normal/location-scale context) hold without modification for a discrete, one-parameter, logit-link family. I have not independently verified R1-R7 for Bernoulli, and I will not claim I have.
defenses.amendment: Narrow the claim throughout: state only that Bernoulli 'demonstrably escapes the known-scale collapse' (a proved, checkable fact), and separately, clearly, that whether the EXACT +1/2 tr(RIV) magnitude applies to a logit-link GLM is an extension not independently verified in this paper -- the measured result is reported as directionally consistent with the general regime, not as confirming a fully-derived +0.5 target.
defenses.residual_risk: The paper's applicability to GLM families more broadly remains an open theoretical question beyond this illustration; flagged as such, not resolved.

defenses.response: Correct, and I withdraw the framing of the 2.2 se gap as a 'match.' I have no attribution for that residual -- no identified finite-sample or higher-order term, no scaling check across N. Calling it 'consistent' overstated what an unexplained 2.2 se departure actually shows.
defenses.amendment: Report the Bernoulli FITTED number plainly as +0.853 (se 0.161), noted as positive and same order of magnitude as the general-case pattern, WITHOUT characterizing it as a confirmation or a resolved match to +0.5. State explicitly that the residual is unattributed.
defenses.residual_risk: A skeptical reader may reasonably conclude the illustration is inconclusive for the exact magnitude, only for the qualitative direction (non-collapse). That is an accurate characterization, not a risk to correct further.

defenses.response: r3#2's literal request names 'the derived trace penalty and design-imbalance terms' and asks whether they 'can be safely generalized to standard GLM frameworks used in applied research' -- and the paper's own text (S4-P8) states plainly that every application (AIC/BIC/LRT correction) uses the estimated-scale regime, never the known-scale collapse. Read against the paper's own scoping of what its applications use, the trace-penalty/general-case result is the operative target of the reviewer's question. But I will not assert this is the ONLY fair reading (see OBJ-08); I will disclose the alternative reading and scope the response accordingly rather than treat the question as fully closed.
defenses.amendment: Add one sentence to the response-letter r3#2 entry naming this scoping choice explicitly: 'This illustration addresses the trace-penalty/IC-correction result the applications use; it does not extend the known-scale collapse's verification beyond the multivariate normal family, which remains an open item (G6).'
defenses.residual_risk: A reviewer could still ask for the known-scale case explicitly; the disclosure makes that a legible follow-up request rather than a silently closed gap.

defenses.response: This is the decisive objection and I concede its specific point rather than rebut it: I cannot produce a blinded, pre-registered, independent re-derivation showing that the '+0.5, general-case' reading was reachable from the theorem condition and the Bernoulli definition alone, without the observed miss prompting a closer look. The record genuinely shows the same advocate, holding the same two inputs, reached the opposite conclusion before data and after -- and I have no documented, timestamped, blinded confirmation that removes the possibility that the miss itself is what motivated the more careful (correct) calculation. I will not claim otherwise; doing so would be exactly the inaccuracy this quorum exists to catch.
defenses.amendment: The manuscript-facing text will NOT claim the +0.5 target was independently pre-derivable in a way that rules out post-hoc motivation. Instead it will state the sequence honestly: a registration error (wrong heuristic) was made, the data missed badly, and a subsequent mechanical check (dH/dp for Bernoulli) -- checkable by any reader right now, independent of who performed it or when -- shows why the original target was wrong. The write-up will not claim this recovers a validated a priori prediction; it will present the corrected reading as a disclosed, timestamped correction of an error, with the underlying calculus offered for the reader's own independent verification rather than as proof of the advocate's foresight.
defenses.residual_risk: A skeptical reader may still discount the corrected reading as motivated reasoning even though the calculus itself is checkable and correct; this is a legitimate residual concern that transparency mitigates but does not eliminate.

defenses.response: Correct: alpha != 0 is necessary but not sufficient for the +1/2 tr(RIV) result to hold exactly. Ruling out the known-scale collapse is not the same as proving the general theorem's magnitude applies unmodified to a logit-link, one-parameter family. I overstated this by presenting '+0.5' as though it followed directly.
defenses.amendment: State the claim at the strength it actually supports: 'Bernoulli's alpha != 0, so the known-scale collapse (0 / -1/2 tr(RIV)) does not apply' is the firm, derivable conclusion. 'The general theorem's +1/2 tr(RIV) magnitude applies exactly to this family' is not independently verified and will be labeled as an untested extension, not a proven consequence.
defenses.residual_risk: None once the claim is stated at this narrower, accurate strength.

defenses.response: I concede that '2.2 se, same sign, same ballpark' was doing the work of a confirmation claim without evidence to support it. There is no named finite-sample or higher-order term, and I have not checked whether the gap shrinks with N or R. Framing it as tolerable noise around a correct target was not warranted by anything I have actually shown.
defenses.amendment: The write-up will report +0.853 (se 0.161) as measured, note it is positive and away from the known-scale collapse's ~0 target, and explicitly flag the ~2.2 se departure from a naive +0.5 general-case comparator as unexplained -- not attributed, not dismissed as noise.
defenses.residual_risk: The illustration's quantitative precision for Bernoulli is now honestly weaker than Gamma's; this is accurate, not a risk to manage away.

defenses.response: This is a fair, live question and I will not claim it is settled. After the correction, both Gamma and Bernoulli test the general case, and the known-scale collapse (the paper's own boundary finding) remains verified only in the multivariate-normal family -- exactly as G6 already discloses, and this Phase-3 work does not close that gap. A defensible scoped reading of r3#2 (see OBJ-04) can treat the applied, IC-correction-relevant trace penalty as the operative target of 'standard GLM frameworks used in applied research,' but I acknowledge a careful reviewer could reasonably read 'current findings' more broadly to include the known-scale boundary result.
defenses.amendment: Add the explicit scope-limiting sentence from OBJ-04's amendment to the Discussion (G9) and the response letter, naming the known-scale-outside-MVN gap as still open rather than implying it was addressed. Do not claim Gamma+Bernoulli 'closes' r3#2 in full; claim they answer the applied-relevance question the reviewer's own language centers on, while flagging the narrower edge-case question as unresolved.
defenses.residual_risk: A reviewer may still ask for a genuine known-scale non-normal exemplar as a follow-up; the disclosure makes that a reasonable next request rather than a hidden gap.

defenses.response: Agreed without reservation, and this is the most important amendment: the 7 se, wrong-sign miss on the Bayesian-draw arm is the single most damaging number to the original registered prediction, and softening it into 'consistent direction' without first stating the miss plainly would be exactly the kind of buried flaw this quorum is built to catch.
defenses.amendment: Every surviving draft states, verbatim and first: 'The originally registered prediction for Bernoulli's genuine Bayesian draw was approximately -0.5 tr(RIV); the measured value is +0.628 (se 0.161), about 7 standard errors away and the opposite sign.' Only after that sentence does the draft explain the entropy-gradient correction and what it does and does not establish.
defenses.residual_risk: None; this is a direct, checkable commitment against the actual file text.

defenses.response: Agreed. The slope-shrinkage follow-up (mean|eta| falling from 0.798 to 0.180, FITTED gap falling from +0.474 to +0.291) was already flagged in my own registration-doc entry as 'not needed to support the headline point,' but the objection is right that even mentioning it alongside the headline risks it being read as corroboration. defenses.amendment: Keep the shrinkage check out of the response letter and Discussion paragraph entirely, or if mentioned in the registration doc for the record, label it explicitly as 'suggestive only, confounded by sampling noise, not evidence for the +0.5 target' and do not cite it in any argument for why the position holds.
defenses.residual_risk: None; this fully removes the weak evidence from any load-bearing role.
